newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Chile, Argentina open Andean gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Argentina open Andean gas pipeline.

text.p: The presidents of Chile, Eduardo Frei, and Argentina, Carlos Menem, opened a $325 million pipeline on Thursday that will pump Argentine natural gas over the Andes to the Chilean capital Santiago.
Frei said the energy link was a clear sign of the economic integration taking place between the South American neighbours.

He and Menem opened a valve to start the gas flow through the 290-mile (463-kilometre) pipeline built by the GasAndes consortium led by Canadian energy firm NOVA Corp and Chilean electricity company Chilgener .
The pipeline will transport 60 million cubic feet (1.7 million cubic meters) of gas a day across the mountains to fuel electricity plants, factories and homes in Santiago.
Chileans hope that the natural gas, which is much cleaner than traditional fossil fuels, will help in the battle against smog in Santiago, one of the world's most polluted cities.

"Our capital and its surroundings suffer serious pollution problems as a result of a combination of climatic factors and contamination from urban life and the growing number of cars," said Frei. "The gas is a fundamental step in efforts to tackle this situation."
The opening of the pipeline coincided with the most serious environmental crisis in years in the city which has suffered dangerous levels of air pollution in recent weeks.
Frei and Menem were due to travel later on Thursday to the San Bernardo district of Santiago to open the reception centre for the gas before its distribution within the city.
NOVA officials said the project, one of the largest ever built by the private sector in Chile, may be expanded over the next decade far more than previously envisaged.

"One of the facets of the gas pipeline business is that when you open up a new pipeline a lot of demand emerges that nobody anticipated," NOVA Corp CEO Ted Newall told reporters after the opening ceremony.
"Over the next 10 years, we're on our way to 700 (million cubic feet of gas) a day, but I'll be awfully surprised if we don't double that."
The GasAndes scheme took 22 months to build through harsh mountain terrain with its owners facing disputes with residents of towns concerned about the safety of the pipeline.
